newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope calls for peaceful solution to East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Pope calls for peaceful solution to East Timor.

text.p: Pope John Paul called on Monday for a peaceful, negotiated solution to the problem of East Timor, the former Portuguese colony which Indonesia invaded in 1975.
"Reflecting on the recent events affecting East Timor, I am hopeful that a more fruitful dialogue will be pursued at all levels," the Pope told Indonesia's new ambassdor to the Vatican.

East Timor, with a population of more than 800,000 people, was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed the next year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which still regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.

"All those who in any way are responsible for East Timor's future must be convinced of the need to arrive as soon as possible at a just and peaceful solution," the Pope said in a written address as the ambassador presented credentials.
"This has been the ardent aspiration of the people there for such a long time," the Pope said.
Last week the Pope encouraged the Nobel peace laureate, Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, to continue his work promoting peace in the territory.
